newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM orders probe into finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM orders probe into finance minister.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius asked the prosecutor's office on Friday to report on the country's young finance minister, who is alleged to have wrongfully accepted a bank loan.

Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas, 29, offered to resign on Thursday after becoming embroiled in scandal over a loan he allegedly obtained on preferential terms from a bank which later went bankrupt.
He said he wanted to quit to avoid damage to the Lithuanian state. Matiliauskas is the youngest member of Vagnorius' right-wing government, which ousted former communists last year.
A statement from the government press office said Vagnorius asked the prosecutor's office to investigate as quickly as possible whether the actions of Matiliauskas were illegal.

"The prime minister will make a final decision on whether to pass the resignation of Rolandas Matiliauskas to the president after the prosecutor's office provides its legal opinion," the statement said.
Allegations surfaced as soon as Matiliauskas was named finance minister last year that he took a loan from the now bankrupt Kredito Bankas on soft terms and did not pay it back.
But Matiliauskas says he handed the loan on to one of the bank's owners and points to a 1996 court decision in which he was not named among the bank's debtors.
Matiliauskas had just taken the helm of the finance ministry and last week announced an ambitious plan to raise a $200 million loan in international markets.
Efforts to get a better credit rating for Lithuania paid off on Friday when rating agency IBCA awarded a BB+ country rating, slightly better than the rating given by Moody's last year.
Vagnorius' government has said it wants to speed the reforms launched after Lithuania quit the former Soviet Union in 1991 and persuade more foreign investors into the country.
